message.content:
The “three great schisms” that most historians point to as the watershed splits in Christian history are:

| # | Schism | Year / Period | Key Parties | Main Consequence |
|---|--------|---------------|-------------|------------------|
| 1 | **Great Schism (East–West Schism)** | 1054 CE | Roman Catholic Church (West) vs. Eastern Orthodox Church (East) | Formal split of the two largest Christian traditions; lasting theological, liturgical, and political differences. |
| 2 | **Protestant Reformation** | 1517–1648 CE | Roman Catholic Church vs. emerging Protestant movements (Lutheran, Calvinist, Anglican, etc.) | Break‑away of numerous Protestant denominations; doctrinal reforms, new ecclesiology, and the reshaping of European religious and political life. |
| 3 | **Old Catholic Schism (19th‑century)** | 1870 CE (after the First Vatican Council) | Roman Catholic Church vs. Old Catholic movement | Separation over papal infallibility and other doctrinal issues; establishment of the Old Catholic Church, which remains in communion with some other churches but independent of Rome. |

These three events are often highlighted because each created a lasting, institutional division that reshaped the Christian world for centuries.
